Running track lanes: why stagger starts?

Goal: I can find arc length as a fraction of circumference.

slides.title: The big idea
slides.html:
Arc length = (arc measure/360) times 2πr.

An arc is a fraction of the whole circle, so its length is the same fraction of the circumference. An arc of 60 degrees in a circle of radius 9 has length (60/360)(18π) = 3π.

On a running track, outer lanes have larger radii, so the curved parts are longer. That is why runners in outer lanes start farther ahead in races with curves: the staggered start equalizes the distance.
